Posts and the person's profile on X, over the v2 API.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own X account in the Gateway, once, and every app that asks uses it. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

The redirect URI to register, with your Gateway's address (like `apps.example.com`):

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/x-oauth/callback
```

OAuth 2 with PKCE on X's v2 API; X's OAuth 1.0a (the v1.1 media upload) stays an app secret.

1. Open [developer.x.com](https://developer.x.com/en/portal/dashboard) and create an OAuth app (also called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Copy the client ID and client secret. The secret is often shown only once.

Add it to your Gateway. It asks for the client ID and secret:

```bash
everyapp provider add x-oauth
```

Or add it in **Manage workspace → Providers**.

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  "x-oauth": { access: "read", scopes: ["posts.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

Apps ask for these scope sets:

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | X account (who you are) | `users.read`, `tweet.read` |
| `posts.read` | Posts and timelines (read) | `tweet.read`, `users.read` |
| `posts.write` | Posts (read and publish) | `tweet.read`, `users.read`, `tweet.write` |

**Check it worked:** `everyapp provider show x-oauth` shows the client as set. Then open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect X**.

Something wrong or missing? [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20X%20%28OAuth%202%29).
